capabilities.name: CircleCI Integration
capabilities.description: Configures CircleCI for continuous integration and deployment. Requires Doppler: the CircleCI MCP server needs CircleCI tokens that are only available through Doppler.

requireStatusCheck.description: Make the pipeline a required status check on the default branch, so a red build blocks the merge (the gate CircleCI contexts used to provide). Set to false to let CI inform without gating.

branchGating.description: Run the heavy pipeline (Lighthouse, preview deploys) on main only by default. Set to false to run them on every branch.

benefits: Automate testing and deployment pipelines
Gain insights with visual build logs and test results
Ensure code quality before merging changes

capabilities.name: Buildkite Integration
capabilities.description: Runs CI on a self-hosted Buildkite agent (Apple silicon) instead of a metered cloud fleet. The pipeline and its GitHub webhook are created during generation, so there is no manual "set up project" step. Can run alongside CircleCI, so a repository can migrate without a flag day.

actions.description: The pipeline is created in the Buildkite organisation during generation
Registers the pipeline GitHub webhook and triggers the first build. Without the webhook, pushes trigger nothing

queue.description: Buildkite agent queue the generated pipeline targets.

provisionPipeline.description: Create the pipeline and register its GitHub webhook during generation. Set to false to only emit the .buildkite/ config.

branchGating.description: Run the heavy gates (Lighthouse, preview deploys) on main only by default. Set to false to run them on every branch.

benefits: Runs on your own hardware — no per-minute metering
No manual setup: the pipeline and its push webhook are provisioned for you
Installs dependencies once per build rather than once per step

capabilities.name: GitHub Releases
capabilities.description: Publishes a GitHub Release when a version tag is pushed. The tag is the trigger, the generated workflow creates and publishes the release with notes, and the release is created with the repository's own token — there is no manual "draft a release" step and no PAT to provision. Independent of CI: Buildkite stays the only validator, and this workflow runs on tags only.

tagPattern.description: Git tag glob that triggers a release. The default publishes any tag starting with "v" (v1.2.3, v2.0.0-rc1).

generateNotes.description: Build the release notes from the pull requests and commits in the release (--generate-notes), classified by .github/release.yml. Set to false to use the annotated tag's message as the notes instead.

draft.description: Create the release as a draft rather than publishing it immediately, so it can be reviewed before it is visible. Set to false to publish on the tag.

prerelease.description: Mark every release as a pre-release: it is not offered as "latest" and not the default download.

benefits: A tag publishes the release — no manual release drafting
Release notes are generated from the merged pull requests
Uses the repository's own token; no PAT to provision or rotate
CI stays on Buildkite — the workflow runs on tags only

capabilities.name: Doppler Secrets Management

actions.description: Add config to shared common project

projectStrategy.description: Where this repo's secrets live: "common" reuses the shared common project (default — no new Doppler project is created); "new" creates a dedicated Doppler project for this repo.

benefits: Centralized secrets management across environments
Eliminate .env files and risk of leaking secrets
Inject secrets securely into your application at runtime

capabilities.name: Docker Container
capabilities.description: Containerize the project and publish to the GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) for deployment to a NAS or self-hosted host via Docker Compose. Mutually exclusive with other deployment systems.

actions.description: GHCR package is created on first push from CircleCI

Create a classic PAT with the write:packages scope (fine-grained PATs cannot access GHCR); add GHCR_USERNAME and GHCR_TOKEN to the CircleCI context. The generated Dockerfile labels the image with its GitHub repo so GHCR links the package to it (public repo -> public package)

publishPort.description: Compose port binding, e.g. "3000:3000" or "127.0.0.1:3000:3000" for a private (Tailscale-only) service. The left-hand side is the published HOST port — Homepage href/widget URLs use it, so "127.0.0.1:3002:3000" yields http://<hostname>:3002/.

baseImage.description: Runtime base image. Defaults to a glibc image (node:22-slim / python:3.12-slim); Alpine only for pure-JS apps.

hostname.description: Hostname used in the Homepage href (defaults to localhost; set to your NAS hostname/IP for browser access).

registryNamespace.description: GHCR registry namespace (GitHub user/org). Defaults to the authenticated GitHub login at generation time.

dataMounts.description: Host data mounts emitted into compose volumes, e.g. [{ "hostPath": "/volume1/data", "containerPath": "/data", "readOnly": true }]. Read-only by default.

aptPackages.description: Debian packages installed in the runtime image via apt, e.g. ["iproute2", "curl"]. curl is added automatically for Python http healthchecks.

envVars.description: Environment variables emitted into the compose environment and .env.example, e.g. ["MCP_PORT=3001"] (a bare key like "MCP_PORT" is filled from .env).

pythonDependencies.description: Runtime Python dependencies (PEP 508 specifiers) emitted into [project] dependencies of the generated pyproject.toml, e.g. ["mcp>=1.2.0", "mcpo>=0.1.0", "httpx>=0.27.0"]. Empty by default; dev tools (pytest, ruff) live in the dev extra.

command.description: Container CMD override (exec form), e.g. ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]. Defaults to a language-appropriate command. A /usr/local/bin/<script> reference is copied from scripts/<script> in the repo (see deploy/README.md).

entrypoint.description: Container ENTRYPOINT override (exec form), e.g. ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]. A /usr/local/bin/<script> reference is copied from scripts/<script> in the repo (see deploy/README.md).

healthcheck.description: Health mechanism: "none", "http:<path>" (e.g. "http:/healthz"; installs curl on Python images), or "command:<cmd>". The Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK and Homepage widget are only emitted when declared. Node web apps default to "http:/health".

language.description: Project language override. Normally derived from the selected devcontainer-* capability; set this only to override it.

armBuilds.description: Also build and publish linux/arm64 images. Defaults to false (x86_64 / linux/amd64 only) — set true when a deploy host (e.g. an ARM NAS or Raspberry Pi) needs arm64 images.

benefits: Deploy to any Docker host (Synology, Unraid, TrueNAS, VPS) — not tied to a cloud vendor
Auto-updates via Watchtower polling the registry
Surfaced in Homepage dashboard with a health widget
Full local/private control of the container
